title: Memory orchestration for KV residency and micro-fragment repair
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce KV cache fragmentation and improve GPU memory utilization for continuous-batching workloads by introducing an allocation orchestration layer that enforces residency policies, micro-fragment repair (lightweight remap), and batching-aware allocation quotas. This ticket scopes design, prototype, and validation on a single-node inference runtime with synthetic and production traces.
acceptance_criteria: New allocator layer can enforce per-model residency hysteresis and reclaim low-value tokens without increasing tail latency >10ms for p95
Micro-fragment repair reduces fragmentation metric (live free-run fragmentation ratio) by >=25% on production LRU traces over 24h
End-to-end per-token cost reduction observed: >=6% in controlled throughput tests with continuous batching enabled
Feature gated and rolloutable: default off, config flags for canary and steady-state
Comprehensive telemetry dashboards and alerts added (fragmentation heatmap, repair rate, repair latency, cache hit deltas)
proposed_solution: Introduce a thin orchestration shim between token allocator and KV manager that implements: 1) residency hysteresis (short-lived soft-reservation windows for recently-populated KV regions), 2) micro-fragment repair as a background, low-priority remap that coalesces small free pools into contiguous ranges using a shadow-copy-and-swap technique, and 3) continuous-batching-aware allocation quotas to avoid over-fragmenting GPU memory under high-concurrency small-batch workloads. The shim exposes knobs for lease length, repair aggressiveness, and batch slot quotas per model variant.
alternatives_considered: Aggressive global compaction: full compaction passes during low-load windows. Pros: predictable fragmentation reduction. Cons: long pauses, complex coordination across shards.
Strict static partitioning: pre-allocate per-model KV regions. Pros: simple, avoids fragmentation. Cons: wasteful for variable workloads and cold-starts.
Realtime relocation on eviction: immediately remap tokens to coalesce on every eviction. Pros: minimal background work. Cons: increases critical-path eviction latency and harms p95.
Reference approach: current opportunistic reclamation + periodic full rewrite (what we run today). Pros: simple. Cons: high fragmentation under continuous small requests.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (prototype): shim + telemetry, implement soft-reservation and batch-aware quotas. Integrate with existing allocator hooks (Alloc/Free) and KV eviction path. Target single GPU node.

Phase 2 (repair): implement shadow remap for micro-fragments. Repair runs as low-priority coroutine that copies live slots into target contiguous region and atomically swaps pointers — avoid moving slots with active KV cursors.
Phase 3 (hardening): add inter-shard cooperate token fencing, ensure correctness with concurrent reads/writes, add unit+stress tests and fuzzing on GPU memory races.
Use existing instrumentation: token residency histograms, slot-age sketches, per-slot owner labels. Add two new counters: repair_ops_completed and repair_ops_abandoned.
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag 'mem_orch_v1' (default off for all customers)
Canary on internal QA cluster with synthetic high-fragment traces (72h)
Small customer pilot: enable for one Dedicated customer with low-risk workload for 2 weeks
Gradual ramp: enable for 10% of production hosts, monitor fragmentation and tail latencies for 7 days before 25%
Full rollout subject to meeting acceptance criteria and no regression on p99 latency
metrics_and_targets: Fragmentation ratio (free_contig_bytes / total_free_bytes) target <= 0.35 (improve from baseline 0.12)
p95 latency regression < 5% and absolute increase < 10ms
Background repair CPU/GPU overhead < 2% of a node's cycle budget during steady-state
Per-token cost reduction >= 6% in steady synthetic load (validated via cost-simulator)
